lede: The maintainer's theme after renderer v3: “I really liked the previous renderer's sharpness for direct lighting, and the temporal stuff has kinda compromised that … reopen the sharpness work but also holistically look at the TAA resolve … and how much of twopointfive's fast-physics noise do we have here?” This page answers it with numbers at all five quality tiers, one recommended configuration per tier, a chaos budget, and the list of legacy paths the answer would let us delete.
rule_html: The decision rule (the maintainer's, applied throughout). “If we don't have great results for sharpness even with lots of dynamic objects, it's fine to make low velocity part of our design principles to get great image quality and performance while only using WebGPU … I'd rather do the slow, methodical stuff great and optimize for the stealth gameplay than compromise that for making the chaos work at all.” So: (1) every variant is RANKED on the calm cases — still + slow-orbit sharpness, edge crawl, static-camera noise, the desk-dim ReSTIR grain, the dynamic-LIGHT scenes (strobe / muzzle flash / torch sweep: light state must never lag), a walking man's shadow — and each tier's configuration is chosen on those alone; (2) the fast-physics scenes do not veto anything: they produce a BUDGET (§6); (3) a fix aimed only at fast occluders would be acceptable only if it cost nothing measurable in the calm cases — none qualified, so none is on by default (§7); E1 (stable-ID motion vectors) is a correctness fix and stays.
intro_html: Three renderers appear throughout: the OLD renderer = every v3 switch off (leader/tail direct light + dtemporal/softblur, temporal + giblur, per-pixel volumetric march, no reflections pass history, native rows + FXAA — pre-v3 main); main = today's defaults (ReSTIR, the v3 denoiser, froxels, TAAU at the tier's scale with the tjank lane's motion terms); and the candidates A–D. Everything new is behind a setting whose OFF is main byte for byte (identity hashes in §9).
instruments_html:
• Sharpness / crawl (__iq.crawl): five straight box edges (the cubicle partition's top strip and its crease, the far keyboard, the V1 keyboard, the manager's desk front) are projected SUB-PIXEL through the camera every frame of a 20-frame 0.3°/frame orbit and of a still take; luma profiles across each edge give the 10–90 % rise width in output px (median over ~150 profiles per edge, then over edges) and the temporal sd of the 50 % crossing's position about the geometric edge = crawl (px; jitter flicker on a still, edge swimming in motion). Plus the high-pass RMS of the V3 desk tile (detail AND noise — the sharp lane's number).
  • Noise (__iq.noise): per-pixel temporal sd of 8-bit luma over 40 still frames in world-anchored tiles (V1 foot penumbra / lit desk / keyboard, V3 desk / chair penumbra / carpet, cubicle desk / chair / worn floor lane, corridor lino + shadow, break-room vending lino / far lino / vending front) + its low-frequency part (sd of an 8-frame running mean: crawl, not grain) + the tjank scenes' desk under the tube held STEADY at 15 % / 100 % and the lamp-lit floor by the window (scene D).
  • Dynamic lights (__iq.dyn, tjank's harness): A the strobing tube (rug / desk lit vs dim means — the reference is 43.9 / 14.9), B the muzzle flash on the gloss lobby floor (flash frame, second frame), C the torch sweep across the corridor haze (froxel means f24‥f34).
  • Fast physics (__chaos): §4.
  • Cost: serialized frames (queue drain + MessageChannel yield per frame), union of the compute passes' timestamp intervals, median / p95 of 100 still frames of the cubicles view (calm) and tjank's stress minute A/B/A/B (QRF weapon lights + rain + 8 smoke domains, orbiting camera).
method_html: Everything ran in a hidden Browser pane on the maintainer's M4 Max while they may have been using the GPU: costs are medians of serialized takes with p95 beside them and interleaved A/B; anything contended shows as a fat p95 and was re-taken where it mattered. Reproduce: PORT=5186 bun run tools/serve.ts + the shot sink on 5187, open /?paused&quality=<tier>&mute, await import('/qa/iq-harness.js'); await __iq.boot(); __iq.tier('<tier>', {batteries, chaos, stress}) (fire-and-forget; poll __iq.tierAt), then python3 tools/qa/iq-report.py --json docs/perf/iq-summary.json && python3 tools/qa/iq-prose.py && python3 tools/qa/iq-page.py. Identity (OFF = main): __sh.identityHash('v3'|'v1') on this branch with every new flag at its default vs main @ 6551c66 served beside it — high v3 c8f100ac / v1 57606578, medium a43a8d44 / 7f73ac88, identical on both trees; re-checked after every commit of the program (E1's motion identity ON included: nothing reorders in a still). Gates: typecheck; tools/qa/gate.sh perf frame-layout level materials player breach glass weather; quality-plan; tour ×2; soak seeds 1,2 × 6 min (+ loud); bun run build; GPU validation scopes clean across the five presets × {sharp, decouple, gbaa, histSharp, motionIds, restir D knobs} × debug views 0–16 × scale steps × preset hops.
frontier_intro_html: One table per tier: every row is a renderer configuration measured with the same instruments on the same boot. Widths and crawl are in that tier's OUTPUT pixels (ultra 2133×1200, high 1777×1000, medium 1600×900, low / verylow their caps — a 2.07-px edge at ultra subtends what a 1.72-px edge does at high). Green = best in column. 'still' crawl ≈ 0.015 is the TAA's jitter flicker on a static edge; ≈ 0.002 is an un-jittered raster. Costs are the calm cubicles still (serialized union median / p95); the stress minute is in §5.
tier_h_html: What high says. Resolution (A) buys almost nothing under TAAU: 0.77 → 1.0 moves the still width 1.84 → 1.81 for +4.1 ms — the resolve, not the raster, sets the sharpness. Sharp direct alone (B) is 1.80 for +1.9 ms. The history de-blur (C2, free) restores MOTION sharpness (1.87 → 1.73; 1.59 at k = 1.0, past the old renderer's 1.63) without touching stills. C3 as first specified — jitter simply off under sharp direct + GBAA — is the crispest still (1.70) with a third less crawl, but stair-steps every hard shadow edge computed at internal resolution and adds 20–35 % penumbra noise (§3 crops); C3j, the DECOUPLED jitter (output raster still, internal raster jittered), keeps GBAA's stability, brings hard shadow edges back smooth, halves the old renderer's crawl (0.108 vs 0.216; main 0.158) and is QUIETER than main on the broad floors — for the same +1.9 ms. C4 (GBAA under a jittered raster) is softer than main and is out. The D rows are the ReSTIR knobs on the noise columns only (sharpness = main's).
tier_u_html: What ultra says. At scale 1.0 there is no internal / output split, so C3 there (c3u = GBAA + jitter off at native rows) inherits C3's two defects (stair-stepped hard shadows, +50 % noise on the worn floor lane). Running ultra at 0.9 with sharp direct + GBAA + decoupled jitter (c3j09) instead gives the C3j picture — crawl 0.161 → 0.104, motion width 1.89 → 1.78, still 2.07 → 2.00, detail 2.91 → 2.92, every noise tile within a few thousandths of main — for the SAME calm cost (20.9 vs 20.8: the internal passes shrink by 19 %, sharpU + compS + gbaa add 2.8) and 1.0 ms less in the stress minute. Spatial reuse everywhere (D2) takes 41 % off the lamp-floor crawl for +1.8 ms; ultra has the headroom but it softens contact shadows where history is old, so it stays a row, not a default.
crops_intro_html: ×3 nearest-neighbour crops, world-anchored (the same texels under every variant): a still after 100 settled frames and the last three frames of the orbit. Read the keyboard's key grid and box edges (sharpness), the monitor stand's contact shadow (hard shadow edges), the keyboard's 2-cm side face (sub-pixel slivers), the partition strip crossing (motion stability), the vending front's backlit blocks (markings at output resolution under sharp direct).

physics_intro_html: Six deterministic scenes, each captured frame by frame under a variant and under a HISTORY-FREE reference render of the very same game frames (the pre-v3 chain at scale 1.0 with every history off: each frame stands alone) — the reference says only WHEN each receiver pixel's true value last changed; every run is then graded against ITSELF: lag = frames from the truth settling until the pixel reaches its own final value (± 8 levels), over 'swept' receiver pixels (reference range ≥ 16 levels; static geometry in every frame of both takes, movers dilated 2 px and excluded); trail = lag × the mover's screen speed; residue +N = |own final − value| N frames after the truth settled, in 8-bit levels (what a trailing shadow edge looks like: +1 ≈ 11 levels is a visible soft smear one frame behind a chair; +8 ≈ 1 is gone); boil = temporal sd of never-swept receivers. Crops: frames +1 / +2 / +4 / +8 after the event, then the lag map (frames, ×32 grey) and the boil map.

chaos_strips.title: P0 · a man WALKING (1.4 m/s) through the fixed torch beam — his shadow on the corridor wall (high)
P4 · desk chair shoved at 3 m/s through the panels' light (high) — the worst calm-adjacent case: an 11-level smear one frame behind
P2 · stun can thrown across the desk-lamp pool at 4 m/s = 40 px / frame (high)
P1 · storage door kicked in, the corridor wedge sweeping the dark floor (high, exposure ×2.5)
P6 · 32 debris boxes tumbling in the aisle (high)

physics_findings_html: Findings. (1) The everyday case is clean: a man walking under the office's broad ceiling panels moves no floor pixel by 8 levels (P0p) — soft emitters make soft, slow shadows and nothing trails; a folding body (P3) is too slow to lag; a can through a haze beam (P2b) leaves under half a level. (2) HARD moving shadows DO trail, at any speed: a man walking through a torch beam (P0) leaves 10–11 levels on the wall for two frames and 7 at +4 (his shadow's trailing edge is a frame or two of soft smear ≈ 10 px behind him); a shoved chair (P4, 2 m/s) 11 / 5 / 2.6 levels at +1 / +2 / +4; a can at 40 px/frame under the desk lamp (P2) only 1.7 / 1.2 / 0.9 (its shadow is small and the lamp's penumbra wide). Lag scales with contrast and edge hardness, not with speed: ≈ 2–7 px of trail per m/s. (3) The kicked door (P1) is fine on the floor (0.4 frames) and shows a one-frame 9-level disocclusion fringe round the leaf itself. (4) 32–64 tumbling shadow-casters (P6) cost +0.03 ms each and add no lag; under C3 WITHOUT jitter they made the whole floor boil (4.2 sd) — the decoupled jitter (C3j) does not (0.38, reference 0.48). (5) C3j reads HALF main's wall residue in P0's first take (5 / 5 / 5 vs 11 / 11 / 8) and WORSE than main behind the shoved chair (P4: 13.5 / 7.9 / 5.1 vs 11.7 / 5.9 / 2.9, lag 3.5 vs 1.8 frames) — read both with care: the mover is still moving when these takes end, and a crisper shadow edge changes each pixel more per frame than a blurred one, which this metric books as residue; the crops and lag maps are here for the eye. Neither number moved the recommendation (rule 1). (6) E1 (stable-ID motion vectors) changes nothing measurable in these scenes: at 40 px/frame a 7-cm can is wholly disoccluded every frame, so its own vector is moot, and receivers never depended on it. It stays as the correctness fix it is (a spawn under a slow tumbling magazine no longer hands it a stranger's transform).
budget_html:
The chaos budget, per tier (what stays under the visible-trail threshold = residue ≤ ~3 levels two frames after the truth, and under the cost bar):

  • Occluder speed is not the limiter — shadow HARDNESS × contrast is. Under the ceiling panels (every room's general light) movers of any speed leave nothing measurable. Under a small hard emitter (torch, desk lamp, muzzle flash) a moving occluder's shadow trails 1–2 frames whatever its speed: ≈ 10 px behind a walking man in a torch beam, ≈ 13 px behind a 2 m/s chair, ≈ 20 px behind a 4 m/s can — 2–7 px per m/s, 5–11 levels for two frames on a hard high-contrast edge, ≤ 2 levels on a lamp-lit desk. Design reading: keep torches and lamps lighting SLOW things (they already do: patrols walk), and let fast things (thrown cans, kicked doors, debris) happen under the panels or in the dark — which is where they happen.
  • Rigid debris: 64 tumbling shadow-casting boxes = +2.0 ms at high (7.9 → 9.9 union), no added lag, boil at the reference's level — inside every tier's bar (high's stress p95 12.3 + 2 < 14 · ultra 26 + ~4 < 30 · medium / low / verylow scale the same +25 % of 'direct'). Call it N ≤ 64 live debris boxes at high and ultra, ≤ 32 at medium and below with BoxWorld's dynamic budget (not the renderer) the real ceiling.
  • Spawn / despawn churn is free with E1 on (identity-keyed vectors); without it a reorder under a SLOW mover would smear its texture for a frame.
  • What would break it: a fast occluder crossing a hard beam close to the camera every frame for seconds (a strobe of disocclusions) — twopointfive's failure mode — is simply not a stealth-game event; the one place it occurs here (the QRF's torches sweeping running men in smoke) is the loud minute the player has already lost.
residuals_html:
• Sub-pixel slivers under C3j (a keyboard's 2-cm side face at 9 m, a paper's edge): dashed / aliased where main's jitter integrates them into a faint line — GBAA cannot antialias what the raster did not draw. Exactly the old renderer's rendering of the same faces; the one visible price of C3j against main. The game's own thin EMISSIVE lines (laser tripwires, weapon lasers, tracer streaks) already widen to a pixel and dim by the same factor; under the decoupled raster that pixel is now an OUTPUT pixel taken at 1.6× the look-at depth (game.ts mPerPx), so beams stay continuous. Static geometry slivers would want the same widening in the level or a conservative edge in the raster; not built.
  • Hard moving shadows trail 1–2 frames (§4). E2 (a velocity-aware history cap on RECEIVERS near fast movers) was not built, and the measurement of its global proxies says a CAP is the wrong lever anyway: halving the shadow denoiser's history (dnShadowCap 12 → 6) or ReSTIR's memory (M 20 → 8) made P0's wall residue WORSE (+1 / +8: 18.4 / 11.5 and 20.5 / 15.8 vs main's 12.3 / 1.9) and P4's no better (11.9 / 3.1 vs 11.7 / 2.9), while adding 10–45 % to the calm penumbra tiles (V1 foot 0.193 / 0.256 vs 0.174) — shorter histories are noisier, the variance clamp that decides how fast a stale shadow is rejected widens with that noise, and the trailing edge stays longer. The lag lives in the clamp's σ under a moving hard edge, so the honest E2 is a motion-aware clamp TIGHTENING for the shadow client (what tjank's motion terms did for the TAA), local to receivers near a mover — a new screen pass to dilate mover velocity, not free by construction. Parked with these numbers; nothing on by default.
  • The lamp-lit floor crawl (ReSTIR, 0.39 sd at high vs 0.08 on the leader path; hundredths of a level per frame): D2 cuts 37–41 % for +0.5 ms (high) / +1.8 (ultra) at the price of softened contact shadows; the real fix is p2a's 'more fresh visibility where the live weight is spread over several partially-visible lights', gated better than 'hint > 0' (D1's blunt version made every tile noisier). Left as rows.
  • The strobe's desk 'grain' is jump dynamics, not grain (steady tube: ReSTIR 0.42 vs leader 0.47) — the authored 14 Hz pattern is the lever (tjank's parked call).
  • F froxel apex / trail / lightning: unchanged from tjank's numbers (apex −25‥30 % at sweep onset, ≤ 13 % two frames behind, the flash's air-glow one frame late by design). A bounded attempt at un-jittering the top light's chord at the apex was not made in this program; documented, not fixed.
  • G contact shadows at internal width under sharp direct (4.9 px at 0.77 vs 3 px native): needs per-light S from the estimator; parked since the sharp lane.
  • C2's de-blur is an unsharp mask on the reprojected history: at k = 1.0 a bright edge in motion can ring by a level or two (it runs in the tonemapped space and the clip bounds it); k = 0.5 showed nothing in any crop. The C2 rows for 'motion clip' made motion width WORSE (2.16) — that knob stays at 0.
tier_m_html: What medium says. Main at 0.67 is soft (2.15 still) and its static edges flicker twice as much as high's (still crawl 0.030). C3j: still 2.15 → 1.59, motion 1.90 → 1.54, crawl 0.151 → 0.095, desk detail 2.16 → 3.57 (+65 %) — sharper in angular terms than main-HIGH (1.59 px of 900 rows vs 1.84 of 1000) for less than main-high costs (6.9 vs 7.9 ms). Raising the scale to 0.77 instead (A) costs two thirds as much and gets a third of the way. C4 (GBAA under the upscale) is 2.64: out.
tier_l_html: What low says. The deeper the upscale the more C3j buys: still 2.18 → 1.50, motion 1.85 → 1.31, crawl 0.152 → 0.084, detail 2.21 → 4.12 (+86 %), for +0.9 ms of output-size kernels — or at ISO-COST by giving back one notch of internal scale (C3j at 0.5: 1.46 / 1.39 / 0.099; the auto ladder does this by itself). Noise is mixed at this depth: quieter on every broad floor (chair penumbra 0.052 vs 0.183, vending lino 0.034 vs 0.213), 15–50 % noisier on the V1 close-up keyboard / foot tiles (fewer internal samples per output pixel and no jitter blur over them). Calm cost takes at this load were contended (fat p95); the stress pairs are clean.
tier_v_html: What verylow says. The same, more so: still 2.42 → 1.43, detail 2.22 → 4.54 (double), crawl halved, +0.5 ms in the stress minute. At a 2× upscale per axis the old resolve simply cannot place a box edge inside two output pixels; the output-resolution raster can.
recommendation_html:
ultra — C3j at 0.9

iq: IQ_C3J, scale 1.0 → 0.9. Sharp direct needs an internal / output split; 0.9 + decoupled jitter + GBAA + de-blur beats native-1.0 TAA on every column (crawl 0.161 → 0.104, motion 1.89 → 1.78, still 2.07 → 2.00, noise tiles within thousandths of main) for the same calm cost (20.8 vs 20.9) and 1.0 ms less in the stress minute (25.6 → 24.6 mean, p95 27.0 → 26.1; bar 30). GBAA + jitter-off at native 1.0 (c3u) is NOT it: stair-stepped hard shadows, +50 % floor noise.

high — C3j

iq: IQ_C3J (0.77 as before). Crawl 0.158 → 0.108 (half the pre-v3 renderer's 0.216), motion width 1.87 → 1.69, still 1.84 → 1.76, desk detail +10 %, hard shadow edges smooth, broad floors quieter than main; a walking man's shadow trails half as much (§4 P0). Cost +1.9 ms calm (7.9 → 9.8); stress minute in §5's table (the sharp lane measured 12.1 → 13.0 p95 for sharp alone; GBAA adds ≈ 0.15; bar 14).

medium — C3j

iq: IQ_C3J. Still 2.15 → 1.59, motion 1.90 → 1.54, crawl 0.151 → 0.095, detail +65 % — sharper per degree than main-high for less than main-high costs. +1.4 ms calm (5.4 → 6.9), stress 7.6 → 9.3 mean / 8.2 → 9.8 p95.

low — C3j

iq: IQ_C3J. Still 2.18 → 1.50, motion 1.85 → 1.31, crawl 0.152 → 0.084, detail +86 %; +0.6 ms stress mean (5.6 → 6.2). On a GPU where that matters the auto ladder gives back a notch of internal scale and keeps almost all of it (C3j at 0.5 = 1.46 / 1.39 / 0.099 at iso-cost).

verylow — C3j

iq: IQ_C3J. Still 2.42 → 1.43, motion 1.94 → 1.43, detail ×2.0, crawl halved; +0.5 ms stress mean.

everywhere

E1 motion identity ON (correctness). ReSTIR / denoiser knobs unchanged (D2 stays a row). ?noiq = the resolve as it was = main hash for hash (high c8f100ac / 57606578, medium a43a8d44 / 7f73ac88 on the final build); ?nosharp drops sharp direct + its riders and leaves the free de-blur. The one taste call before merging: sub-pixel slivers (§3's keyboard crops) render as on the OLD renderer, not as on main.

legacy_html:

Every v3 'off' switch is today both an identity A/B against pre-v3 main and one leg of the OLD-renderer reference these instruments use (__iq 'old', tjank's allOff, __chaos REF); deleting any of A–D ends in-tree reproduction of pre-v3 main, and before A or D go the chaos reference must be re-defined on v3 (restirHistory 1, direct history 0, Temporal flag off, froxelHistory 0, TAA reset per frame).

tldr_html: One configuration wins every calm-case column at every tier: C3j = sharp direct + DECOUPLED jitter + GBAA + the history de-blur (ultra run at 0.9 so sharp direct is live). Widths in each tier's OUTPUT px (lower = sharper); crawl = edge-position sd in motion (lower = stabler); detail = high-pass RMS of the desk tile (higher = crisper); costs on the M4 Max, serialized union. The one visible price against main is sub-pixel slivers rendering as on the pre-v3 renderer (§7). Fast physics: hard moving shadows trail 1–2 frames at ANY speed under small emitters and nothing trails under the panels — a budget, not a veto (§6).
